subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: Help me understand what's in these airline reviews — I'm not sure which aspect is most worth analyzing.

judge.implied_focus: Expressed customer dissatisfaction in the review text — i.e., what aspect customers complain about most, how negative the review tone is, and whether that text sentiment aligns with the numeric ratings.

per_column.name: sentiment_score
per_column.rationale: A compound sentiment (~-1..1) of the review text. It relates to the 'how negative is the review' facet, but on its own it is exactly the kind of bare/generic sentiment measure the rubric flags — it points at the focus only weakly.

per_column.name: dominant_complaint
per_column.rationale: Core column: extracts the primary complaint theme (staff, delay, seat, food, value, entertainment). This is the substantive, data-inferable anchor of the focus and directly answers 'which aspect is worth analyzing.'

per_column.name: review_length
per_column.rationale: A purely mechanical token/word-count metric. It does not center on any substantive dissatisfaction concept and reads as grab-bag filler rather than a facet of the focus.

per_column.name: rating_sentiment_gap
per_column.rationale: Compares text sentiment to the numeric rating, a genuinely analytical relational facet — surfaces where written tone diverges from scores, tying text signal back to the structured ratings and reinforcing the dissatisfaction focus.

judge.rationale: Three of the four columns (dominant_complaint, sentiment_score, rating_sentiment_gap) loosely orbit a single coherent concept — dissatisfaction/complaint content expressed in the review text and its alignment with ratings — so the set is not wholly scattered. However, coherence is diluted: sentiment_score is bare sentiment and review_length is a mechanical text-length metric, precisely the generic signals that do not realise a focus. As a structure, there is a promising nucleus (a complaint theme + an intensity measure + a text-vs-rating gap) but it is half-filled with undifferentiated filler rather than a clean, differentiated facet/predictor set, so structure quality is only moderate. The strongest inferable focus — complaint-driver themes — is genuinely actionable (an analyst can prioritise staff/delay/seat issues and probe text-rating divergence), but because the column set as a whole leans partly on vacuous sentiment/length framing, actionability is only moderately supported rather than strong.
